text: Name a champion whose full official name is four letters or fewer
rule: Count only the letters in the champion's official name.

text: Name a champion who can become invisible
rule: One of the champion's own abilities makes them Invisible or Camouflaged, even if only after an upgrade or evolution (e.g. Kai'Sa's evolved Supercharge).

text: Name a champion with a dash or leap (blinks and teleports don't count)
rule: One of the champion's own abilities moves them quickly across the ground or through the air to a location or target: dashes, leaps, lunges and hops all count.

text: Name a champion who can pull an enemy
rule: One of the champion's own abilities forcibly moves an enemy toward the champion or toward a point (hooks, pulls, drags).

text: Name a champion who can stun
rule: One of the champion's own abilities Stuns an enemy, including conditional stuns (e.g. into a wall).

text: Name a champion who can knock up an enemy
rule: One of the champion's own abilities Knocks Up (airborne in place or lifted) an enemy.

text: Name a champion with a global ultimate
rule: The champion's own ultimate (R) can reach any point on the map: unlimited range or map-wide effect.

text: Name a player who won Worlds
rule: Any player listed on the winning team's roster at any World Championship so far (Season 1 onward), substitutes included. Coaches don't count. Leaguepedia's roster is the source.

text: Name a ranged champion who can become invisible
rule: A ranged champion where one of their own abilities makes them Invisible or Camouflaged, even if only after an upgrade or evolution. Ranged means a base attack range of 300 or more; transforming champions count by their base form (Kayle, Gnar and Jayce are melee, Nidalee and Elise ranged).

text: Name a melee champion who can pull an enemy
rule: A melee champion where one of their own abilities forcibly moves an enemy toward them or toward a point (hooks, pulls, drags). Melee means a base attack range under 300; transforming champions count by their base form (Kayle, Gnar and Jayce are melee, Nidalee and Elise ranged).

text: Name a ranged champion who can knock up an enemy
rule: A ranged champion where one of their own abilities Knocks Up an enemy. Ranged means a base attack range of 300 or more; transforming champions count by their base form (Kayle, Gnar and Jayce are melee, Nidalee and Elise ranged).

text: Name a ranged champion with a global ultimate
rule: A ranged champion where their own ultimate (R) can reach any point on the map. Ranged means a base attack range of 300 or more; transforming champions count by their base form (Kayle, Gnar and Jayce are melee, Nidalee and Elise ranged).

text: Name a champion who can both dash and become invisible
rule: Both apply: one of their own abilities makes them Invisible or Camouflaged, even if only after an upgrade or evolution, and one of their own abilities dashes, leaps, lunges or hops them to a location or target (blinks and teleports don't count). The two can come from different abilities.

text: Name a champion who can both pull and stun an enemy
rule: Both apply: one of their own abilities forcibly moves an enemy toward them or toward a point (hooks, pulls, drags), and one of their own abilities Stuns an enemy, including conditional stuns. The two can come from different abilities.

text: Name a champion who scales infinitely (stacks with no cap)
rule: One of the champion's own abilities grants permanent stacks with no maximum that keep increasing a stat or damage for the rest of the game.

text: Name a champion whose ultimate deals no damage
rule: Casting the champion's own ultimate (R) never damages an enemy by itself: it only crowd-controls, buffs, heals, shields, moves, transforms or empowers their next attacks or abilities. Damage dealt by a unit the ultimate summons counts as damage.

text: Name a champion with a three-hit passive or ability
rule: One of the champion's own abilities triggers an effect on every third attack, hit or cast, or when three hits or stacks land on the same target. Items and runes don't count.

text: Name a champion who can reveal stealthed enemies
rule: One of the champion's own abilities reveals enemies even while they are Invisible or Camouflaged (True Sight, or revealing a target through stealth).

text: Name a champion who can create a wall enemies can't walk through
rule: One of the champion's own abilities creates terrain or a barrier enemies can't walk through: an impassable wall, pillar, ring or arena. Walls that only slow, stun or damage enemies walking through don't count.

text: Name a champion who can become untargetable
rule: One of the champion's own abilities makes them Untargetable, even briefly or only mid-cast, including Stasis. Invisibility and invulnerability don't count.

text: Name a champion with an ability that resets or refunds on a takedown
rule: One of the champion's own abilities has its cooldown reset, refunded or reduced, or can be recast, when the champion gets a takedown (kill or assist) on an enemy champion.

text: Name a champion whose resource bar isn't Mana (Energy, Fury, Heat...)
rule: The champion's resource bar is something other than Mana (Energy, Fury and the like). Champions with no resource bar don't count.

text: Name a champion who can cheat death or keep fighting after dying
rule: One of the champion's own abilities lets them keep acting after dying, or stops or reverses their own death. Invulnerability alone and items don't count.

text: Name an item named after a person or character
rule: The item's name contains the name of a person or character from League's world, usually as a possessive. Roles, creature types, groups (a giant, a warden) and places don't count.

text: Name a champion whose name is exactly two words
rule: Words are the space-separated parts of the champion's official name, so an abbreviation or a numeral counts as a word, and Nunu & Willump (three parts) doesn't count.

text: Name a champion with an apostrophe in their name
rule: The champion's official name contains an apostrophe ('). Other punctuation, such as a full stop or &, doesn't count.

text: Name a champion whose name contains a Z or an X
rule: The letter Z or X appears anywhere in the champion's official name, not only at the start.

text: Name a champion whose name is one syllable
rule: The champion's official name is said as a single syllable in standard English pronunciation.

text: Name a champion whose name has 10 or more letters
rule: Count only the letters in the champion's official name, across every word; spaces and punctuation don't count. Wukong has 6.

text: Name a champion whose name starts with A, E, I, O or U
rule: The champion's official name starts with A, E, I, O or U. Y doesn't count.

text: Name a champion with a double letter in their name
rule: The same letter appears twice in a row anywhere in the champion's official name, ignoring case. A repeated syllable like Lulu's doesn't count.

text: Name a champion who rides a mount, vehicle or ally to get around
rule: The champion gets around riding something that carries them: a mount, steed, mech or aircraft, an ally, or the terrain itself.

text: Name a champion who wears a mask or helmet (base skin)
rule: On their base skin the champion's face is covered by a mask, helmet or visor. Blindfolds don't count.

text: Name a champion who isn't humanoid (beasts and monsters)
rule: On their base skin the champion is not humanoid: a beast, monster, bird, construct or creature without a human-like body plan (two arms, two legs, upright).

text: Name a champion who uses a gun
rule: On their base skin the champion fights with a gun or firearm: pistols, rifles, cannons, shotguns, rocket launchers.

text: Name a champion who floats or flies instead of walking
rule: On their base skin the champion floats, hovers or flies instead of walking on the ground.
